claims.claim_text: The indexed Darcy Buffard is a high-confidence match to André Germain Buffard, whose official BCRA file inventory gives René Darcy as his service name.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official French inventory combines the index surname Buffard with the BCRA name Darcy; a separately compiled mission chronology places the same names in OSS/G2 service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the unusual exact Buffard-Darcy name combination, the official BCRA identity/alias pairing, and independent OSS mission context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The BCRA inventory covers wartime service and the corroborative mission chronology is dated September 25, 1944; neither establishes a pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: The index appears to preserve the service name as a first name. Box 91 should confirm the alias linkage and pre-OSS chronology.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Andrew P. Bugay is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name, middle initial, and private identifier match across the OSS index and official Army-entry file; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private identifier and exact normalized full name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army-entry record is dated December 29, 1942; the index does not provide an OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: Namesakes lacking the private identifier or Box 91 linkage were rejected.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry, Andrew P. Bugay was recorded in the miners and mining-machine operators occupational group.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official record carries code 721, which NARA's numerical list maps to miners and mining-machine operators.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private identifier and full indexed name.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to Army entry on December 29, 1942; the relation to OSS recruitment is unknown.
claims.match_notes: No employer, mine, machine, location, exact duties, or immediate OSS predecessor is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Howard Bugbee is a probable match to Howard C. Bugbee, documented in 1936 Goodrich employment and in 1944 as an attaché at the American Embassy in London.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Howard C. Bugbee, Attaché American Embassy at London.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary alumni notice and an official wartime diplomatic record share the uncommon Howard C. Bugbee name and provide a coherent 1936-1944 chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable from the uncommon exact first and last name, consistent middle initial in two independent dated sources, and wartime government context; the OSS index omits the middle initial.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish 1936 employment and a 1944 diplomatic role but do not state when he entered OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Box 91 must confirm the middle initial and OSS linkage before the identity is promoted to high confidence.

claims.temporal_assessment: The conflicting Army record cannot establish Delmas A. Bugelli's chronology, occupation, or employment.
